REPORT
Subject: REPORT ON THE ARREST OF FOUR SUSPECTS AT 227 CHEFIANG ROAD.
Made by: J. L. R. Forwarded by: C. I.

Sir,

Questioning of the four suspects
1) MA ZU SAI (馬如山),
2) ZHIG TSOU SAI (陳佐山),
3) PU SHI TING (浦世疃),
4) HSU SHU HAO (徐樹豪),
has been continued at C. I. D. by C. I. D. and the undersigned since the date of their arrest (7.3.39) by members of the Japanese Military at No. 227 Chefiang Road.

Perusal of their fingerprints shows that the 2nd. named ZHIG TSOU SAI (陳佐山) was charged with possession of firearms on 30.7.27 and sentenced to 8 months imprisonment. He was released on remission of sentence on 19.2.28. In that instance he claimed he was a victim of circumstances. He has no further convictions. The other three have no previous convictions.

The 1st. named MA ZU SAI (馬如山) has continued in his asseverations that he is as related in his initial written statement, namely, a rice merchant who was visiting Shanghai together with his wife. Nothing has been unearthed which would show that he was definitely concerned with guerillas.

The 2nd. named ZHIG TSOU SAI (陳佐山) has likewise reiterated as given in his written statement and nothing has been forthcoming to refute same or show that he is concerned in guerilla activities.

查阅他们的指纹显示，第二名嫌疑人 ZHIG TSOU SAI（陳佐山）曾于 1927 年 7 月 30 日被控持有枪支，并被判处 8 个月监禁。他于 1928 年 2 月 19 日因减刑获释。在那次案件中，他声称自己是环境所迫的受害者。他再无其他定罪记录。其他三人无前科。

    With reference to the chop marked Wu Dee (武田)
found on the person of the 3rd. named POO SZ TSUNG(浦士宗)
he claims that it is the property of a Japanese known
to the staff in the recording office Chautoong Road
(肇通路), Chapei, by that name. He (POO SZ TSUNG)
also works in the building and found the chop outside
the office on the roadway at about 4 p.m. on the 6th.
March, 1939 and, the staff having gone, he continued
into the Settlement as was his intention and meant handing
same back to the Japanese known as Wu Dee (武田) on the
7th. March, but was unable to do so owing to his arrest.
    The fact of him being found in possession of
the chop at the time of arrest by the Japanese Military
Police led the latter to suspect that he had either stolen
same or had one made and was using it to chop counterfeit
passes. This is denied by him. He denies being concerned
in guerrilla activities.
    Amongst the effects of the 4th. named ZEE ZU
HSUIN (徐樹) was a slip of paper bearing the
characters "A hut we three go to arson (草棚我三人放火)"
    Questioned re this he stated that he had three
straw huts in Tung Kya Pang, Kiangchow which were used
to store hay and straw inside and, on visiting same
towards the end of December, 1938 found they had been
burned down. Sticking to one of the unburnt doors he
found the slip of paper and retained same.

    关于在第三名嫌疑人 POO SZ TSUNG（浦士宗）身上发现的刻有“武田”字样的印章，他声称该印章属于闸北肇通路（Chautoong Road）记录办公室工作人员所知的一位名叫武田（Wu Dee）的日本人所有。他（POO SZ TSUNG）也在该大楼工作，并于 1939 年 3 月 6 日下午 4 点左右在办公室外的道路上发现了这枚印章，当时工作人员已离开，他便按原计划进入租界，打算在 3 月 7 日将其归还给那位名叫武田（Wu Dee）的日本人，但因被捕而未能如愿。
    他在被日本宪兵队逮捕时身上藏有该印章，这一事实导致后者怀疑他要么偷窃了该印章，要么伪造了一枚并用于盖印假通行证。他对此予以否认。他否认参与游击队活动。
    在第四名嫌疑人 ZEE ZU HSUIN（徐樹）的物品中，有一张纸条，上面写着“草棚我三人放火”几个字。
    就此接受讯问时，他声称他在江苏江桥镇（Kiangchow）东家浜（Tung Kya Pang）附近有三间草棚，用于内部储存干草和稻草，而在 1938 年 12 月底去查看时，发现它们已被烧毁。在其中一扇未烧毁的门上，他发现了这张纸条并保留了下来。

The following is the statement of MA KYING SZ ( ), M/Female, 22,
native of Tsing-pu taken by Mr. C.D.C. 2

My husband, Ma Zu Sei, and myself together with a
neighbour (female) left Tsing Jiao at about 7 a.m. 6.3.39 and
arrived in Shanghai at about 12 noon same date, putting up
residence at Room 225, Heng Yui Hotel, 227 Chekiang Road.
At about 6 a.m.(7.3.39) the following morning, three
strangers in foreign clothes came into our room, and whilst
two of them conducted a search the other one spoke to my
husband, saying that "someone" had reported to the Japanese
Authorities that my husband was a member of a mobile unit.
They then made an attempt to drag my husband away, saying that
he would be sent to the authorities concerned to be dealt with
accordingly. However, during the attempt, they advised my
husband to hand over to me for safe keeping the following
articles (1 gold ring, one $5-note, one $1-note and one "Omega"
watch), which my husband had on his person, saying that should
those articles be brought to the offices of the Japanese
Authorities, they would be "confiscated". My husband did so
at once and handed everything over to me, whereby two of them
went away with my husband, leaving the remaining one to guard
our neighbouring woman and myself. (The latter woman was not
the one who had come to Shanghai with us, but another one who
lived in some other room at the same hotel and was brought to
be detained with me in my room). About 30 minutes later,
someone outside called our guard to the telephone. He came
back in a few seconds, saying that he had to bring the other
woman and myself to their office. He further said that we

I am a native of Wong Ka Jau, Wongtu Village,
Tsingpu.

During August 1938 I removed to Kong Jau Village,
(on boundary of Shanghai and Kading) with my concubine, Ma
Kyung Sz, aged 22 years. There we occupied a room of the
house belonging to one Li Ai Mau, situated in the back street
of the Southern area.

At about 7 a.m. 6-3-39, I came to Shanghai with my
concubine, carrying a sum of $415.00 with us. We put up in
Room 225 at the Mang Yuen Hotel, Hupeh Road. At about 2 p.m.
the same day I proceeded to Fokien Road Bridge, where I
handed the $415.00 to my native friend, Woo Zau Tsaung, on a
boat, with a request that he would bring rice to Shanghai for
sale. I then returned to the hotel, being prepared to get back
to my native country at noon on the 7-3-39. Unexpectedly,
at about 6 a.m. 7-3-39 three strangers dressed in foreign
clothes called at my room, and one of them showed a pass to
me, stating that they were despatched by the Japanese to
conduct investigations into the fact that we were members of
a guerilla unit. Ignoring my repudiation of their remarks,
they compelled me to go out with them. We were just on the
point of leaving the room when one of the visitors told me to
hand my money, pocket watch, gold finger ring etc., to my
concubine. This was complied with, and they told me that they
were helping me by not taking my concubine into custody. They
then took me to the E. Tai Garage, Hupeh Road, where I was made

U.B.R. Consul.          7.3.39              Clerk Hsu.

My name is Sung Tsoo Sai, age 35, native of Kading
near Nanziang, married, cotton and bamboo merchant, re-
siding Zung Dien, Nanziang, Kading Hsien.

I was born in Zung Dien, Nanziang, Kading Hsien on the 11th
day of the 4th moon 1905.

My father, Sung Yen Ching ( 〔此处转录不清〕 ) is now aged 72
and has resided in my native place all his life. My mother
died 14 years ago.

I have only one older and one younger sister who are
now married and are living on the outskirts of Shanghai.

I have never received any Military training whatsoever,
neither have I had any political training. I am not a guerrilla
neither have I at any time had anything to do with them.

My schooling has been of a very elementary nature. I
went to the village primary school between the ages of 7 and 11.

My father is a farmer and had about 13 mow of land. On
leaving school I assisted him until I was 15 years of age.
I then secured employment as a coolie with a Mr. Lambert(?)
(at that time employed by B.A.T.) residing 8 Hart Road and
stayed for 4 years.

Mr. Lambert (?) then introduced me to a Mr. Hutchinson(?)
residing 2 Love Lane as an assistant boy. I stayed there for
4 months and left only because my master went on home leave. He
however, secured me employment with a Mr. MacDonald(?) of the
Mercantile Bank of India, as a boy. I worked there for 19
months when Mr. MacDonald(?) went to Japan and I then return-
ed to my native place and assisted my father.

嘉定                                      D.S. Fowler
UBR 领事。          1939年3月7日              书记员徐。

我叫宋佐才，35岁，南翔附近嘉定籍人士，已婚，棉竹商人，居住于嘉定县南翔镇众典村。

我于1905年农历四月十一日出生于嘉定县南翔镇众典村。

我的父亲宋延清（Sung Yen Ching）〔此处转录不清〕现年72岁，一生居住在家乡。我的母亲于14年前去世。

我只有一个姐姐和一个妹妹，她们均已婚，现居住在上海郊区。

我从未接受过任何军事训练，也没有受过任何政治训练。我不是游击队员，任何时候都与他们没有任何关系。

我所受教育非常基础。7岁至11岁期间，我在村立小学读书。

我的父亲是农民，拥有约13亩土地。离校后，我协助父亲劳作，直到15岁。随后，我在哈特路8号居住的兰伯特先生（Mr. Lambert(?)）（当时受雇于英美烟草公司 B.A.T.）处谋得一份苦力工作，并在那里待了4年。

后来，兰伯特先生（?）将我介绍给爱文义路2号居住的哈钦森先生（Mr. Hutchinson(?)）做助理听差。我在那里待了4个月，离开的原因仅是因为我的主人回家休假。不过，他随后为我争取到印度商业银行（Mercantile Bank of India）麦克唐纳先生（Mr. MacDonald(?)）处的听差工作。我在那里工作了19个月，直到麦克唐纳先生（?）前往日本，我便返回家乡协助父亲。

page_data.en:

At 22 I married my wife, and started on my own in the
cotton and bamboo business. I also assisted on the land.
From the age of 22 until the present time I have
continued doing like wise.
People residing near my home know of me doing business
in cotton and bamboo and therefore have sold their small
stocks to me and I have brought it to Shanghai and resold
it.
At about 9 a.m. on the 6th March 1939, I left my home
on foot to come to Shanghai for the purpose of having a
bath and haircut etc. On reaching Chung Shan Road I was
stopped by a Japanese sentry who forced me to move wood
etc for him. I was allowed to go at about 12 noon. I went
a teashop in Tseu Ka Wei and rested until about 4 p.m. and
then continued to I-Chang Road Bridge where I boarded a No.
19 Route trolly car and proceeded to Peking - Chekiang Roads.
I had a bath at the Foo Lung Zeu ( **〔此处转录不清〕** ) Bath House,
Chekiang Road and then proceeded to a barber shop also on
Chekiang Road.
After having a haircut I went for food to a foodshop
on Chekiang Road and, on leaving at about 8 p.m. and walking
along Chekiang Road near Nanking Road, I met one known to me
as POO ( **〔此处转录不清〕** ) (also arrested). He is not an intimate friend
of mine.
Poo is or was employed by the Shanghai City Government
as a tax-collector.
Poo asked me what I was doing in Shanghai, and, after
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

22岁时，我娶妻，并开始独立经营棉竹生意。我也继续在土地上劳作。
从22岁至今，我一直如此生活。
住在我家附近的人都知道我做棉竹生意，因此将他们的小批量存货卖给我，我再将其运到上海转售。
1939年3月6日上午9时许，我步行离家前往上海，目的是洗澡、理发等。到达中山路时，我被一名日本哨兵拦下，强迫我为他搬运木材等物。中午12时许，我被允许离开。我去曹家渡的一家茶馆休息至下午4时许，然后继续前往宜昌路桥，在那里乘坐19路电车前往北京路与浙江路路口。我在浙江路的福龙池（Foo Lung Zeu）**〔此处转录不清〕**浴室洗了澡，然后前往浙江路的一家理发店。
理完发后，我去浙江路的一家食品店用餐，晚上8时许离开，沿浙江路靠近南京路地段行走时，遇到一位我认识的人，名叫蒲（POO）**〔此处转录不清〕**（也被逮捕）。他并非我的密友。
蒲当时或曾受雇于上海市政府担任收税员。
蒲问我在上海做什么，在

explaining what I had done, and saying that I was going
to hire a small room in a lodging house for the night and
return home the next morning, Poo said that he and a friend
had engaged room No. 238 in the Hung Yuen (宏源) lodging
House, Chekiang Road, and that I might share same if I
wished.

I thanked him and accompanied him to the lodging house.
On arrival in room No. 238 I saw another male, name unknown,
but who was introduced to me as Tien (田). I, being tired,
was given a bed cover and I went to sleep on the floor.

At about 6 a.m. on the 7th March, I was awakened by
a knocking on the door. I arose and opened same and was
confronted by three male Chinese; one wearing long black
Chinese style overcoat and two wearing dark coloured foreign
style suits and overcoats.

The three males entered the room and ordered Poo and
Tien to get up. After ordering us to dress they asked which
of the three of us was named Lau (刘). We all denied
knowing anyone by that name where upon two of the three
went out and returned a few minutes later saying they had
located Lau but that we had better sit down and wait for
a while.

A few minutes later, the three ordered we three occupants
to go downstairs with them. Arriving there we were met by
a party of males some of whom I recognised as Japanese.

We were told to get into a m/car together with one
of the three male Chinese who had entered the room of the

我解释了我的行程，并说打算在客栈租一个小房间过夜，次日早晨回家后，蒲说他和一位朋友已经在浙江路宏源（Hung Yuen）客栈预订了238号房间，如果我愿意，可以同住。

我向他道谢，并随他前往客栈。到达238号房间后，我看到另一名男子，姓名不详，但被介绍为田（Tien）。我因疲倦，得到一条床罩，便睡在地板上。

3月7日上午6时许，敲门声将我惊醒。我起身开门，面对三名中国男子；一人身穿黑色长款中式大衣，另外两人身穿深色西装和大衣。

这三名男子进入房间，命令蒲和田起床。在命令我们穿好衣服后，他们问我们三人中谁是刘（Lau）。我们都否认认识叫这个名字的人，于是三人中的两人走出去，几分钟后回来说他们已经找到了刘，但我们最好坐下等一会儿。

几分钟后，这三人命令我们三名住客随他们下楼。到了楼下，我们遇到一群男子，其中一些人我认出是日本人。

我们被告知与之前进入客栈房间的三名中国男子中的一人、另一名不知名的中国男子以及三名日本男子一起坐进一辆摩托车。其中一名日本人驾驶车辆。

lodging house, and another unknown male Chinese, and three
male Japanese. One of the latter drove the car.
On arrival at Central Station our names were called
out by one of the three Chinese who had arrested us. On
him calling Mau, the unknown male Chinese answered to that
name. He answered ours as they were called.
A short time later we were taken to Louza Station
and again, a short time later, taken back to Central Station.

Signed:

At about 10 p.m. yesterday (6.3.39), when passing the
Wing On Co. on Chekiang Road, I happened to meet my native
friends, Lee Zu Hsuin and Tung Tsoo Sai, who took me to Room 238
of Meng Yui Hotel on Hankow Road. As it was rather late when
we met, I did not go home and stayed there for the night.
At about 6 a.m. this early morning, when we were still
in bed, 3 Chinese in foreign clothes visited our room, saying
that they had been sent over to conduct a search on the room
by Japanese Authorities, who had reasons to believe that all
three of, Lee, Tung and myself were members of a mobile unit.
After the search of the room, they took us to the E.Tai Garage,
where we boarded a hire-car and proceeded to gate of the Central
Police Station, where the three of them were seen talking to
two Japanese, after which we were taken to Louza Police Station,
from where we were again taken to Central Police Station - Crime
Branch Headquarters.

This is the truth.

以下为蒲世宗（POO SE TSUNG）〔此处转录不清〕之供词，24岁，市政府官员，隶属闸北分局，住址为杰斯菲尔德路（Jessfield Road）旁高克扎102号，嘉定籍人士，由本人于1939年3月7日在C.1讯问室录取，由书记员叶（Yeo）传译。

昨晚（1939年3月6日）10时许，当我经过浙江路的永安公司时，偶遇同乡好友李祖信（Lee Zu Hsuin）和董佐才（Tung Tsoo Sai），他们带我到汉口路孟园旅馆（Meng Yui Hotel）238号房间。由于相遇时天色已晚，我没有回家，便在那里过夜。
今天清晨6时许，当我们还在床上时，三名身穿西装的中国人来到我们的房间，称他们受日本当局派遣来搜查房间，日本当局有理由相信李、董和我三人均为流动部队成员。搜查房间后，他们将我们带至东泰车行（E.Tai Garage），我们在那里登上一辆租赁汽车，前往中央捕房门口，在那里看到那三人与两名日本人交谈，随后我们被带往老闸捕房，之后又被带回中央捕房——总部刑事科。

此为实情。

签名：蒲世宗。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of ZEE ZU HSUIN (徐祖信), 32, M/Ex-teacher,
native of Shanghai, residing Room No.238 Meng Yui Hotel, Hupeh Road.
taken by me C.l on the 7. 3. 39 and interpreted by Clerk Yao

I was formerly employed as a teacher at the Kiang Jiao
Preparatory School, Kiang Jiao Village, Shanghai, until the
13.8.37 when I lost the job owing to hostilities.

On the 5th. of November, 1938, I obtained the position
of an assistant in the King Jiao Guild, which was operated by
the Japanese Authorities.

Yesterday, from Nanziang, I boarded the Dah Zuh Bus
and came to Shanghai, putting up in Room 238 Meng Yui Hotel,
Hupeh Road. As I was purchasing a pair of rubber shoes along
Chekiang Road, I happened to encounter two of my native friends
Zung Tsoo Sai and Poo Sz Tsung, who were subsequently taken
to my room. Owing to late hours, they stayed in my room for
the night.

At about 6 a.m. this morning, when we were still abed,
three men in foreign clothes visited our room, accusing us of
being members of mobile units and conducted a search in the
room. Soon, we were taken to the E. Tai Garage where we
boarded a hire-car and proceeded to the Central Police Station.
After a short while, we proceeded to Louza Station, but soon
we were taken back to Central Police Station - Crime Branch
Headquarters for questioning.

This is the truth.

Signed : ZEE ZU HSUIN

警务调查报告。

以下为徐祖信（ZEE ZU HSUIN）之供词，32岁，男，前教师，上海籍人士，居住于湖北路孟园旅馆238号房间。由本人于1939年3月7日在C.1讯问室录取，由书记员姚（Yao）传译。

我此前受雇于上海江桥村江桥预备学校担任教师，直到1937年8月13日因战事失业。

1938年11月5日，我在由日本当局经营的江桥公会（King Jiao Guild）获得一份助理职位。

昨天，我从南翔乘坐大中华巴士（Dah Zuh Bus）来到上海，入住湖北路孟园旅馆238号房间。当我在浙江路购买一双胶鞋时，偶遇两位同乡好友宋佐才（Zung Tsoo Sai）和蒲世宗（Poo Sz Tsung），随后他们被带到我的房间。由于时间已晚，他们在我的房间过夜。

今天早上6时许，当我们还在床上时，三名身穿西装的男子来到我们的房间，指控我们是流动部队成员，并对房间进行了搜查。很快，我们被带至东泰车行，在那里登上一辆租赁汽车，前往中央捕房。过了一会儿，我们被带往老闸捕房，但很快又被带回中央捕房——总部刑事科接受讯问。

此为实情。

签名：徐祖信
